votes.item_title: Item 15: Consolidated Annexation, Utility Extension, and Initial Zoning — Oaks at Lyons Farm
votes.notes: 9.4 acres on Scott King Road; initial Rural Residential (RR) zoning for up to 17 single-family homes.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented the utility extension agreement, voluntary contiguous annexation, and initial Rural Residential zoning for 17 single-family homes on 9.4 acres on Scott King Road, noting a positive fiscal impact analysis. Lyons Farm resident Jeff Dozier opposed the plan on behalf of Silver Pine Court residents because all traffic would exit through their neighborhood rather than adding a direct entrance to Scott King Road. Developer Jarrod Edens responded that the conservation subdivision preserved 50% open space (4.7 acres) and that NCDOT discouraged an additional state-road driveway, while Transportation staff confirmed a Scott King Road entrance would likely require costly left-turn lane and vertical-curve grading. Planning staff clarified that voluntary neighborhood meetings were not mandated for annexations, and Council unanimously approved the item 7-0 with the applicant's voluntary $1,500-per-student contribution to Durham Public Schools.

votes.item_title: Item 16: Consolidated Annexation, Utility Extension, and Initial Zoning — Richmond Park
votes.notes: RS-10 with development plan for 15 single-family detached lots.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented the utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation, and RS-10(D) initial zoning for 15 single-family detached lots, carrying forward a 2009 county-approved 16-lot subdivision with one lot removed. Adjacent neighbors Matthew Willis, Charles Cheney, and Bill Hunt objected to multi-day stormwater runoff not captured by single-day 100-year storm models, potential mosquito breeding in the retention pond, and the absence of a tree buffer along the northern property line. Applicant attorney Michael Birch explained that the wet detention pond and level spreader would reduce post-development runoff below pre-development rates up to the 100-year storm and noted the site complied with UDO buffer rules. Following questions from Mayor Bell and Council Member Don Moffitt, the applicant proffered a 10-foot undisturbed tree buffer along the northern boundary, and Council approved the item 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Consolidated Annexation — RTP Global Mission Church (BDG-130016)
votes.notes: Initial Industrial Light (IL) zoning permitting a place of worship by right.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented the utility extension agreement, voluntary contiguous annexation, and initial Industrial Light zoning for the RTP Global Mission Church site, noting adequate utility capacity and net-positive fiscal impact in the second year after build-out. Church member Stephen Park represented the congregation alongside Pastor Lee and offered to answer questions. Council Member Don Moffitt asked staff about steep slopes toward an adjacent stream on the property, which staff confirmed existed. With no public speakers in opposition, Council closed the public hearing and approved the item 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Consolidated Annexation — Grovery NC
votes.notes: Non-contiguous annexation and RS-20 zoning for one single-family lot.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff recommended approval of a utility extension agreement, voluntary non-contiguous annexation, and initial RS-20 zoning for the Grovery NC parcel to allow one single-family home. Applicant representative Cliff Cradle explained that the lot bordered the city limits and was too small to accommodate private well and septic systems, prompting the request for city utilities. No council members raised objections and no members of the public spoke in opposition. Council closed the public hearing and approved the request 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Consolidated Annexation — Changing Hearts for Changing Lives (BDG-130017)
votes.notes: Initial Rural Residential (RR) zoning; proposed place of worship remains subject to Board of Adjustment minor special use permit.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented the utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation effective December 31, 2013, and initial Rural Residential zoning for Changing Hearts for Changing Lives, noting that revenues were not projected to exceed expenditures within 10 years for a place of worship and that the church use would still require a minor special use permit from the Board of Adjustment. Council Members Diane Catotti and Don Moffitt confirmed that driveway access would need NCDOT approval and that Planning Commission had a standing resolution approving matching initial county-to-city zoning. Neighbor David Johnson questioned who would pay for sewer extension along Medallion Drive and raised stream drainage concerns, and staff confirmed the applicant pays utility costs and must meet 50- to 100-foot stream buffers and stormwater standards. Council approved the item 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Comprehensive Plan Amendment — Page Park 2 (A13-0006)
votes.notes: FLUM change on ~10 acres from Office to Medium Density Residential.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented Lennar Carolinas' application (A13-0006) to amend the Future Land Use Map designation of an approximately 10-acre parcel from Office to Medium Density Residential. Staff noted the amendment created an appropriate land-use transition between planned industrial/commercial uses to the east and lower-density residential to the north, and reported an 11-0 recommendation for approval from the Planning Commission. Applicant representative Robert Shunk of Stewart Engineering spoke briefly in agreement with the staff report. With no public opposition, Council approved the plan amendment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Zoning Map Change — Page Park 2 (Z13-0017)
votes.notes: 16.87 acres on Jessup Street rezoned to RS-M(D) for maximum 124 residential units.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented the companion rezoning of 16.87 acres on Jessup Street to Residential Suburban Multifamily with a Development Plan (RS-M(D)) for up to 124 units, noting an 11-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Council Member Steve Schewel noted the rezoning was projected to add up to 20 students to Durham Public Schools and asked whether the applicant would proffer $500 per additional student, citing the Southpoint Trails precedent. Applicant representative Robert Shunk indicated they planned to build townhomes (estimated 15-17 additional students) and formally proffered $500 per additional student determined at site plan. Schewel also confirmed with staff that the 100% impervious surface allowance reflected Crabtree Creek Basin rules outside a water supply watershed, though stormwater treatment still applied, before Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 22: Comprehensive Plan Amendment — Muirfield Commercial (A12-0015)
votes.notes: FLUM reconciliation on 1.85 acres on Guess Road from Low/Medium Density Residential to Commercial.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented Horvath Associates' application to amend the Future Land Use Map for 1.85 acres on the east side of Guess Road between Horton Road and Victory Boulevard from Low/Medium Density Residential to Commercial. Applicant Ron Horvath explained that the site had been zoned commercial in 2003 before the city routinely reconciled the comprehensive plan alongside rezonings. Council Member Don Moffitt confirmed with staff that the request served as a technical reconciliation of the 2003 zoning with the Future Land Use Map. Following an 11-0 Planning Commission recommendation and no public opposition, Council approved the amendment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 23: Zoning Map Change — Muirfield Commercial (Z12-0026)
votes.notes: CN(D) modification on 2.95 acres at 1439 Victory Blvd.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented a Commercial Neighborhood development plan modification for 2.95 acres at 1439 Victory Boulevard expanding permitted non-residential floor area from 5,000 to 8,000 square feet, modifying site access, and allowing a mix of office, retail, and non-drive-through restaurant uses. Applicant Ron Horvath highlighted that the revised plan eliminated two stream crossings and rear access through the adjacent residential neighborhood by shifting driveway access to Victory Boulevard. Council Member Diane Catotti confirmed that the 2003 graphic commitment for the Warren Creek Trail easement on the adjacent parcel remained binding. With an 11-0 Planning Commission endorsement and no opposition, Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 24: Zoning Map Change: Hudson Property (Z13-0010)
votes.notes: Rezoning 7.99 acres at 117 E NC 54 Hwy from RS-20 to OI(D) for up to 150,000 sq ft of office space.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented Davis Moore Capital's application to rezone 7.99 acres at 117 East NC 54 Highway from RS-20 to Office and Institutional with a Development Plan for up to 150,000 square feet of office space, including transit improvements and a 4-foot bicycle lane. Bob Zumwalt of McAdams represented the applicant. Council Member Steve Schewel questioned Transportation Assistant Director Wesley Parham about adding 4,500 daily trips near congested I-40 and Fayetteville Road; Parham testified that NC 54 traffic (16,000 trips) remained well below Level of Service D capacity (27,200) and the site lacked direct access to I-40 or Fayetteville Road. Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 25: Zoning Map Change — Hope Valley Farms Pod BB Revisions (Z13-0012 / Murphy USA) (Initial Vote)
votes.notes: Initial vote prior to reconsideration to add brick exterior commitment.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented Murphy USA's request on 6.77 acres at 1051 Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway to remove 2009 proffers barring fuel sales and convenience stores and to remove redundant roadway commitments already built by others. Attorneys Patrick Byker and Lewis Cheek emphasized a 0.8 opacity landscape buffer, 500-foot separation from the nearest townhomes, and $2 million in new tax base. Elm Grove Townhouse Association representative Aida Len O'Tougou requested a continuance because HOA board elections delayed neighborhood review, though Planning staff verified that first-class mail notices were sent to 45 nearby owners and the Elm Grove HOA in April. Following debate over notice and neighborhood compatibility, Council initially approved the rezoning 5-2 with Diane Catotti and Don Moffitt voting no.

votes.item_title: Motion to Reconsider Item 25 (Hope Valley Farms Pod BB Revisions / Murphy USA)
votes.notes: Reconsideration requested after council members noted design commitments did not require brick exterior.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after the initial 5-2 vote on Item 25, council members questioned whether the Murphy USA convenience store building was required to have a brick exterior as they had been told. Planning staff read the existing 2009 design commitment, which permitted stucco, precast concrete, fiber cement, vinyl, or metal panels in addition to brick. On advice of the City Attorney, a member on the prevailing side moved to reconsider the action so the applicant could amend the design commitment on the record. Council voted 7-0 to reconsider Item 25.

votes.item_title: Item 25: Zoning Map Change — Hope Valley Farms Pod BB Revisions (Z13-0012 / Murphy USA) (Re-vote as Amended)
votes.notes: Final approval of Murphy USA rezoning with four-sided brick exterior commitment.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the 7-0 motion to reconsider Item 25, Murphy USA's representative formally amended the project's design commitments on the record to require that all four exterior walls of the convenience store building be brick, excluding windows, doors, and trim, and agreed to email the revised commitment to Planning staff the next morning. With that added commitment in place, Council took a new vote on the rezoning. The amended rezoning passed 5-2, with Diane Catotti and Don Moffitt maintaining their no votes.

votes.item_title: Item 26: Street Closing — North LaSalle Street (SC13-00003)
votes.notes: Closure of 150 linear foot segment of N. LaSalle Street right-of-way for Sheetz site plan.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented Withers & Ravenel's request (SC13-00003) to close a 150-linear-foot segment of North LaSalle Street right-of-way that had long been used as parking for an adjacent property, enabling Sheetz Inc. to use the area for parking and side access to a new convenience store and gas station under site plan review. Staff confirmed that city agencies, NCDOT, and utility providers identified no service delivery impacts. Sheetz representative Jamie Gerhardt spoke briefly in support, and no opponents appeared. Council closed the hearing and approved the street closing 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 4 (Pulled): Workforce Investment Act Youth Contract with Community Partnerships, Inc.
votes.notes: Pulled by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden over 0.5-point scoring edge over Durham-based Operation Breakthrough.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden pulled Item 4 to question why the WIA youth contract was recommended for Raleigh-based Community Partnerships, Inc. (score 89) rather than Durham-based Operation Breakthrough (score 88.5), arguing the city should better mentor and support local contractors. Workforce Development senior manager Michael Honeycutt and Youth Program Coordinator James Dickens explained that the Durham Workforce Development Board recommended CPI based on strong federal performance compliance, and that the six-month contract included up to two years of renewal options. Council Members Steve Schewel and Diane Catotti, who attended the Workforce Development Board meeting, noted that an audit of Operation Breakthrough and concerns about its reliance on rotating six-month interns heavily influenced the board's vote. Mayor Bell voiced sympathy for supporting local firms and noted Operation Breakthrough was not present to respond, before Council approved the contract 6-1 with Cole-McFadden voting no.

votes.item_title: Item 10 (Pulled): 2014 Financial Crimes Task Force Grant
votes.notes: Pulled by resident Victoria Peterson.
votes.discussion_detail: Resident Victoria Peterson pulled Item 10, a $23,000 U.S. Department of the Treasury Financial Crimes Task Force grant with a $3,800 supplement, to raise concerns about police leadership and allege that certain younger officers had seized cash from residents' homes as alleged drug money without proper courthouse accounting. She asked the City Manager for a five-year report on seized drug funds and questioned why existing seizure funds could not pay for task force expenses. Mayor Bell responded that individuals with specific allegations must bring formal evidence directly to the City Manager rather than relying on hearsay at the podium. Council then moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the grant 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 11 (Pulled): Amendment to Fitness Medical Risk Training Contract for Psychological Services
votes.notes: Pulled by resident Victoria Peterson.
votes.discussion_detail: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 11, an amendment to the police psychological services contract with Fitness Medical Risk Training, praising officer counseling while urging Council to add funding to hire a board-certified psychiatrist for active crisis scenes. Referring to the recent fatal shooting of Derek Walker during a mental health crisis, Peterson argued that a licensed psychiatrist should be deployed to speak with individuals in distress when family members and clergy are kept back. Mayor Bell stated her comments would be taken into consideration. Council then unanimously approved the contract amendment 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Hope Valley Farms Pod BB Rezoning for Murphy USA Fuel Station & Convenience Store (Z13-0012)
disagreements.summary: Council split 5-2 on removing a 2009 prohibition on fuel sales and convenience stores at 1051 Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway after neighboring Elm Grove Townhouse residents requested a continuance and council members scrutinized building aesthetics.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the rezoning (with an added four-sided brick exterior commitment) without further delay.
side_a_arguments: City and applicant met all statutory notification rules, including first-class letters to 45 property owners and the Elm Grove Townhouse Association.
The site has been zoned Commercial General since 2009, lies 500 feet from the nearest townhomes behind a 0.8 opacity vegetative buffer, and adds $2 million in tax base.
Applicant amended design commitments on reconsideration to mandate a brick exterior on all four walls.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose approval or delay action in light of Elm Grove neighborhood concerns.
side_b_arguments: Questioned whether affected Elm Grove townhome residents had adequate opportunity to review the proposal given their HOA board transition.
Raised compatibility and neighborhood impact concerns for the convenience store and fuel station.
disagreements.resolution: Initially passed 5-2, reconsidered 7-0 to secure a four-sided brick exterior commitment, and re-approved 5-2.

disagreements.issue: Awarding WIA Youth Contract to Out-of-County Provider Over Durham Applicant (Item 4)
disagreements.summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden dissented against awarding a Workforce Investment Act youth contract to Raleigh-based Community Partnerships, Inc. over Durham-based Operation Breakthrough.
disagreements.side_a_position: Follow the Workforce Development Board's recommendation to award the contract to Community Partnerships, Inc.
side_a_arguments: CPI scored higher overall (89 vs. 88.5) and consistently met federal and state WIA performance goals.
Workforce board members cited a recent audit of Operation Breakthrough and concerns about continuity under Operation Breakthrough's six-month intern staffing model.
disagreements.side_b_position: Prioritize Durham-based contractors and invest in mentoring local organizations rather than awarding contracts outside the city.
side_b_arguments: A half-point scoring margin (89 vs. 88.5) should not outweigh keeping public workforce dollars with a local Durham provider.
City staff should proactively mentor local firms like Operation Breakthrough so they can compete effectively for city contracts.
disagreements.resolution: Contract awarded to Community Partnerships, Inc. by a 6-1 vote.

disagreements.issue: Police Transparency, Racial Disparities in Traffic Stops, and Critical Incident Disclosures
disagreements.summary: During the third-quarter crime report, council members and residents debated how aggressively the Durham Police Department should release information and address racial profiling concerns amid pending SBI investigations.
disagreements.side_a_position: Demand faster public disclosure of critical incident facts and non-defensive reform of traffic-stop and policing practices.
side_a_arguments: Public confidence in police truthfulness and transparency requires timely answers on the Jesus Huerta, Derek Walker, and Jose Ocampo cases rather than months-long waits.
FADE's traffic-stop and search disparity statistics require open-minded review and concrete reforms.
Community activist Victoria Peterson called for replacing the Police Chief over homicides, lawsuits, and mental health crisis handling.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defend the Police Department's record while respecting independent SBI, Medical Examiner, and District Attorney investigative processes.
side_b_arguments: Part 1 crime is at a 14-year low and the vast majority of officers serve fairly without bias.
Underfunding of the SBI crime lab and Chief Medical Examiner delays limit what factual information the city can legally and ethically release before investigations conclude.
Chief Lopez urged community members to come forward with information on street violence rather than waiting solely on police.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote; council members expressed support for ongoing Human Relations Commission hearings and police internal review reforms while awaiting SBI findings.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting December 2, 2013
meetings.executive_summary: The December 2, 2013 organizational meeting featured an extended tribute to retiring Ward 2 Council Member Howard Clement III after more than 30 years of service, followed by the swearing-in of Mayor Bill Bell, re-elected Council Members Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel, and newly elected Ward 2 Council Member Eddie Davis. Council unanimously re-elected Cora Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore and issued proclamations for Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day while recognizing the Police Department's CALEA accreditation. In regular business, Council approved the consent agenda 7-0, extended UDI Community Development Corporation's economic development incentive agreement 6-0 (with Mayor Bell abstaining), and extended PSNC's natural gas franchise agreement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Tribute to Howard Clement III and Swearing-In of Mayor and Council Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Eugene Brown paid tribute to outgoing Ward 2 Council Member Howard Clement III for more than three decades of civic leadership, and Clement delivered farewell remarks. District Court Judge Pat Evans administered oaths of office to Mayor Bell, Council Members Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel, and incoming Ward 2 Council Member Eddie Davis, each of whom gave brief inaugural remarks.

agenda_items.title: Election of Mayor Pro Tempore
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell recommended that Ward 1 Council Member Cora Cole-McFadden continue serving as Mayor Pro Tempore for the new council term. Council moved, seconded, and unanimously confirmed Cole-McFadden before taking a brief recess.

agenda_items.title: Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day Proclamation and DPD CALEA Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon reconvening, Mayor Bell presented the Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day proclamation to El Centro Hispano and the Bill of Rights and Immigrant Solidarity Committee, reaffirming Durham's 2003 resolution protecting residents regardless of immigration status. Council also recognized the Durham Police Department's national CALEA accreditation honors.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-2, 4-11, 12-15, 17-19)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda headings, including board appointments, the Strategic Plan performance audit, FY 2014-15 budget development schedule, WIA dislocated worker contract amendment, SAMHSA behavioral health grant, Durham County tax interlocal amendment, solid waste collection trucks, fire apparatus maintenance interlocal agreement, City Hall exterior renovations, radio support equipment, HUD fair housing agreement, 21C Durham license agreement, and water compliance contracts.

agenda_items.title: Amendment to Economic Development Incentive Agreement with UDI Community Development Corporation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell recused himself from voting and turned the gavel over to Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden. Office of Economic and Workforce Development staff member Chris Dickey recommended extending UDI CDC's capital investment completion deadline to February 4, 2014 and contract expiration to June 1, 2014 due to delays beyond UDI's control; no public speakers objected.

agenda_items.title: Public Service Company of North Carolina (PSNC) Gas Franchise Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an extension of the natural gas franchise agreement with Public Service Company of North Carolina (PSNC), originally executed in 1981. With no council questions or public speakers during the public hearing, Council closed the hearing and approved the extension.

agenda_items.title: Council Committee Assignments and Human Relations Commission Alternate Liaison
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell noted proposed committee assignments and relayed Council Member Don Moffitt's request for a second council member to serve as an alternate liaison to the Human Relations Commission during its upcoming deliberations. Council Member Steve Schewel volunteered to serve as alternate, and members clarified that liaisons provide advice and report back to Council without voting.

votes.item_title: Election of Cora Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore
votes.notes: Recommended by Mayor Bill Bell following the swearing-in ceremony.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the swearing-in of Mayor Bill Bell, re-elected Council Members Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel, and newly seated Ward 2 Council Member Eddie Davis, Mayor Bell exercised his prerogative to recommend Cora Cole-McFadden to continue serving as Mayor Pro Tempore. Bell praised Cole-McFadden's steady support and partnership during his tenure. A motion and second were made without opposition or debate. Council confirmed Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore by a unanimous 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Item 22: Amendment to Economic Development Incentive Agreement with UDI Community Development Corporation
votes.notes: Mayor Bill Bell recused himself due to employment with UDI CDC; Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell stepped aside from presiding and stated he would not vote on Item 22 due to his affiliation with UDI Community Development Corporation, handing the gavel to Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden. Chris Dickey from the Office of Economic and Workforce Development explained that UDI CDC faced project delays largely beyond its control and recommended extending the capital investment completion deadline to February 4, 2014 and the overall contract expiration to June 1, 2014. No council members asked questions and no public speakers appeared during the public hearing. Council approved the amendment 6-0 with Mayor Bell abstaining.

votes.item_title: Item 23: Public Service Company of North Carolina (PSNC) Gas Franchise Extension
votes.notes: Extension of natural gas franchise agreement originally entered in 1981.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff presented Item 23, an ordinance extending the city's natural gas franchise agreement with Public Service Company of North Carolina (PSNC), which was originally established in 1981. Mayor Bell opened the public hearing and invited public comment, but no members of the audience asked to speak on the item. Following the brief staff presentation and closure of the public hearing, Council approved the franchise extension unanimously 7-0.
